fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"One Damaged Medieval Manuscript","body":"Garton walks the chain of custody behind the King James Revelation and argues it narrows to a single late medieval Greek copy, the commentary manuscript now catalogued as minuscule 2814, carrying marginal notes attributed to Andreas of Caesarea and dated only by handwriting style to the twelfth century. Erasmus worked from that damaged copy while assembling his Textus Receptus, and because its final six verses were missing he filled the gap by translating backward out of Jerome's Latin Vulgate. Garton finds it bitterly ironic that the closing warning against adding to the prophecy was itself, on this account, an addition."},{"title":"The Convenient Trinity Verse","body":"Saccoccio reads out the better documented case, 1 John 5:7, the one verse that states the doctrine of the Trinity outright. Erasmus left it out of his first two Greek editions because he could find it in no Greek manuscript, only in later Latin copies, and after being attacked by Stunica and the Archbishop of York he reportedly promised to include it if anyone produced a single Greek witness. One promptly appeared in Britain, the Codex Montfortianus, which scholars now widely regard as forged to win the argument. Saccoccio contends such timely discoveries were the rule, not the exception."},{"title":"Athanasius and the Canon Anchor","body":"Both hosts note that the familiar 27 book New Testament first appears as an authoritative list in the 39th Festal Letter of Athanasius of Alexandria in 367. Garton stresses that those letters do not surface in complete form until 1842 and that the oldest fragments are ninth or tenth century, while Athanasius himself also commends Wisdom, Sirach, Judith, Tobit, the Didache and the Shepherd. In the same letter he condemns heretics who write books when they choose and assign them a date so they may pass as ancient, which Garton treats as an admission that backdating was routine."},{"title":"Chasing a River With No Water","body":"Saccoccio's refrain is provenance, the fountain nobody bothers to trace, and Garton illustrates it by pushing one plain English sentence through repeated machine translation into Latin and back until the meaning quietly drifts. Now scale that, they argue, to centuries of monks copying metaphor and idiom by hand. Garton also questions the standard claim that the apostles wrote in Greek to reach the widest audience, given literacy estimates of three to ten percent in the first century, and floats the possibility that Jerome's Latin came first. The printing press, he says, froze a fragmentary tradition into one seemingly flawless book."},{"title":"Heresy as Criminalized Choice","body":"Garton locates the deepest shift in the move of the sacred from public rites to private belief, citing Fustel de Coulanges, Arthur Melzer, and Rousseau's line that obligatory dogma leaves a field of battle always open among men. The Greek word hairesis, he notes, once meant only a choice or leaning between schools, stoic or epicurean, and carried no shame, until it was inverted into the crime of choosing wrongly. Irenaeus aimed Against Heresies at the Gnostics and Valentinians, and Garton argues the same machinery still runs under secular names, with cancellation standing in for excommunication."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The Apocalypse is nightmare fuel when taken literally. Is the Book of Revelation real? Join Chance Garton and Dylan Saccoccio on Inner Whirled for a decode of the Revelation Mind War and the origins of the Textus Receptus. We document how the Dutch humanist priest Erasmus heavily altered scripture to create the basis of the King James Version (KJV), including the controversial Comma Johanneum and the forged Codex Montfortianus. This episode explores how the transition from outward ritual to inward belief created a persecutory psychology and a lasting war for the mind that persists in modern society.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Jesus Admits He Is the Morning Star", "body": "In Revelation 22:16, the verse Erasmus back-translated from Jerome's Latin because Minuscule 2814 was missing its ending, Jesus names himself the bright and morning star. Chance traces the Latin thread outward: 2 Peter has Lucifer rising in your hearts, Job asks whether you can bring forth Lucifer in his time, and Isaiah 14:12 puts a fall from heaven and a morning star in the same breath, which is the whole basis for the devil legend. Read together, the figure dogmatic Christians revile turns out to be the celestial body Christ claims as his own."}, {"title": "The Goddesses Behind the Virgin Mary", "body": "The second half stacks up the pagan mothers standing behind the Madonna. The Orphic hymn crowns Aphrodite queen of heaven and the cosmos, Sappho's ode reads like a Hail Mary, and Stella Maris appears nowhere in the Vulgate but only in the late Middle Ages. Then come the birth stories: Kybele born from spilled seed on a rock, castrated by frightened gods, her severed parts producing an almond tree that impregnates the nymph Nana, and Myrrha turned into a myrrh tree that gives birth to Adonis, the annually dying and rising lover of Venus."}, {"title": "The Androgynous Savior in the Almond", "body": "The mandorla, the almond shaped aureole around Mary in Christian art, is the same almond as the Cybele story and an unmistakable image of the female generative organ. Chance points out that Jesus appears inside it too, sometimes without his mother, which raises the question of what a bearded Aphrodite is doing in a womb. Macrobius describes a bearded Venus in Cyprus, bearded goddesses turn up across antiquity, and the conclusion drawn is that esoteric Christianity never held Jesus and Mary apart at all. They are one figure, the great mother father, creator and destroyer."}, {"title": "The Case Against John of Patmos", "body": "Eusebius would not say the apostle wrote Revelation, pointed instead to a second John the presbyter at Ephesus, and preserved Dionysius of Alexandria's finding that the polished Greek of the gospel and the broken Greek of the apocalypse cannot share a hand. Patmos never appears in any Roman record as a penal colony, the archaeology shows fishing villages and temples, and the Domitian persecution that supposedly put John there reads as a fourth and fifth century literary invention. The Council of Laodicea, Cyril, Gregory of Nazianzus and the Syriac Peshitta all left the book out."}, {"title": "Farrago and the Cobbler's Bible", "body": "Dylan's word for the surface confusion is farrago, the mixed fodder thrown to livestock, and both hosts argue that trying to force Lucifer, Jesus, Satan, Aphrodite and the planet Venus into one consistent system is exactly the trap. Look for connections, they say, and refuse to get attached to interpretations. The episode closes on the irony that Erasmus scolded Luther for handing the mysteries to cobblers while himself omitting and restoring the Trinity verse, back-translating Latin into Greek, and leaving ninety alterations in Revelation alone. He cobbled together a Bible for the cobblers."}]

He thinks he's Jesus.”", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you try to find the water, you find out that the water wasn't there, and neither is the fountain which it flowed from.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "A hippie named John having a psychedelic trip is the whole reason we've got this crazy apocalypse-obsessed culture.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The time of Christ is not something that you'll ever find in the historical record.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "They point at other people and accuse them of doing the evil that they themselves do.", "author": "Dylan Saccoccio", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/0d1bec4c-36ec-4ba4-a1cb-9de0908b2433/Dylan-Saccoccio.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text":"The book of Revelation has for its origin one late medieval Greek manuscript.","author":"Chance Garton","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"When you actually try to chase that illusory river, that maya if you will, you find out there is no water and there is no fountain.","author":"Dylan Saccoccio","portrait":""},{"text":"This portion of the text that millions of Christians regard as the original and literal word of God was actually a 16th century Dutch priest's reconstruction of Greek from a Latin original.","author":"Chance Garton","portrait":"https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"},{"text":"You have no right to force Santa Claus's history on me.","author":"Dylan Saccoccio","portrait":""},{"text":"People believe that Christianity happened and then the church formed because of Christianity. That is not the case.
